title: Italian biathlete undergoes heart surgery after dropping out of Winter Olympic race
content:
Italian biathlete Tommaso Giacomel has undergone “successful” minor heart surgery after he pulled out of the 15km mass start at the Winter Olympics with breathing and movement problems.

A statement issued by the Italian Winter Sports Federation (FISI) on Tuesday said electrophysiological study done at the Galeazzi Hospital in Milan “revealed an electrical conduction abnormality in the atrium”. FISI confirmed Giacomel, 25, had “completely successful” ablation surgery, a procedure which is used to treat irregular heartbeat.

“Tommaso will be discharged on Thursday morning and in two weeks will undergo further scheduled tests which, once passed, will allow him to return to regular training,” the statement added. His CT scan, MRI scan, and maximal exercise tests were all “normal”.

Giacomel said in a post on Instagram: “My season is over. Gutted.”

Giacomel had led the race on Friday, but slipped behind and eventually pulled out. He later said in a social media post that he was “really struggling to breathe and to move” following the second prone, and that having to end his race prematurely was the “worst feeling I have ever experienced in my life so far”.

He added: “I tried to ski really slow the first part of the third lap but my body wasn’t allowing me to ski anymore. A lot is going through my head at the moment… frustration, anger, disappointment… It’s devastating. It’s devastating to stop but there wasn’t anything I could do against my own body today.”

In the opening week of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics, Giacomel was part of Italy’s mixed relay team which won a silver medal, with France taking gold. He came into the Games in good form, having won his fourth individual World Cup race of the season and third in succession in Oberhof.

He is second in the overall World Cup standings, 37 points behind leader Eric Perrot.
